cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Karma – the sum of a person's actions in this and previous states of existence, viewed as deciding their fate in future existences.

p.em: Example: She believes that helping others brings good karma back to her life.

cosy-blockquote.p: Festering – becoming worse or more intense, especially through long-term neglect or indifference.

p.em: Example: Leaving an argument unresolved leads to festering resentment between friends.

cosy-blockquote.p: Boulder – a large rock, typically one that has been worn smooth by erosion.

p.em: Example: The sudden financial crisis felt like a massive boulder crushing his plans.

cosy-blockquote.p: Crush – to deform, pulverize, or force inwards by compressing forcefully.

p.em: Example: The heavy weight of his mistakes threatened to crush his confidence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Defeat – an instance of defeating or being defeated; failure to win or succeed.

p.em: Example: Accepting defeat gracefully is an essential step toward future improvement.

cosy-blockquote.p: Self-pity – excessive, self-indulgent, and self-centered sorrow over one's own sufferings.

p.em: Example: Instead of wallowing in self-pity after the setback, she started looking for solutions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Shards – pieces of broken ceramic, metal, glass, or stone, typically having sharp edges.

p.em: Example: She carefully swept up the shards of the shattered glass vase.

cosy-blockquote.p: Deceive – to deliberately cause someone to believe something that is not true, especially for personal gain.

p.em: Example: It is never a good idea to deceive the people who support you.

cosy-blockquote.p: Deserve – to do something or have or show qualities worthy of reward or punishment.

p.em: Example: Everyone makes mistakes, but we all deserve a second chance to fix them.

cosy-blockquote.p: Folly – lack of good sense; foolishness.

p.em: Example: It was complete folly to believe that his lies would never be discovered.

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
